trickyParts: The plan expected /worker/ready's confirming get_state to drive the retry through the client's idle transition; it cannot: onIdle -> promoteWorkerQueue reads queue[0] synchronously before queueUnstartedPrompt has pushed the token. All three not-started paths therefore retry on the next drain (idle/dead event or the 60 s sweep) and never immediately; processes.test.ts A5-ready asserts exactly that.

awaitTurnStart checks receipt.hasStarted after the get_state instead of parsing data.isStreaming itself: the client settles the receipt from an isStreaming:true answer, so there is one definition of 'turn observed'. The fake client mirrors that (getState with isStreaming:true starts the pending receipt).

In the real-tmux e2e the third failure's retirement makes the shim socket close, onWorkerClientClosed's reconnect is refused, and markWorkerDead's promoteWorkerQueue cold-launches the queued assignment on its own — so the test asserts the property (no fourth prompt, launch attempted) rather than a launch count. The fake client reconnects to itself, which is why the unit test needs an explicit fourth drain.

A superseded receipt never settles: a later prompt() on the same client replaces the one slot, so a late start after a retry was sent resolves the retry's receipt, not the first one; commitLateStart compares the task by value so either path commits the same delivery once.
deviations: Added a second commit (208d87937e58) not in the plan: ProcessManager's role notices (worker-queued, worker-started, worker-died, launch-failed, revive-failed, redelivered exception payloads) were published with a bare nats.publish that the Envoy listener rejects as an invalid envelope, so none ever reached an architect; the dep is now publishRole, wired to envoyPublish. Found because the rig listener logged the rejection at the exact moment the promoted prompt committed. The boot-redrive index.test.ts case asserts the architect's worker-started arrives through envoyPublish.

Added SMOKE_NATS_NAME and SMOKE_WORKER_CAP to scripts/smoke/up.sh (and SMOKE_NATS_NAME to down.sh, both documented in the README): the container name was hardcoded, so a second rig could not run beside LEGION-44's, and worker_cap was hardcoded to 6 where the plan's recipe needs 1.

The rig's daemon API contract is 1 on this branch while the installed profile plugin is 1.23.0 / contract 2 (main moved on); rather than rebase (forbidden except on a conflict) the rig ran a dedicated OMP profile with the plugin built from this commit — the deployment rule for a contract skew. The branch will need main's contract-2 plugin only after it merges into main; nothing in this change touches the LegionDaemonApi shapes.

The negative control's queued entry was hand-authored in state.json (pendingAssignment + queue push) while the daemon was stopped, not produced by a live spawn_worker: the plan's recipe already hand-edits the same claim's locator, and after the positive path no worker held the slot, so a live spawn would have taken the direct resumed path instead of queueing.

findings.finding: A ready-time prompt (workerReady -> promptExistingWorker) whose shim socket closed before the turn started was handled as a swallowed prompt: boot confirmed, task queued, promptFailures counted. The socket-close handler had already snapshotted the claim as unconfirmed and routed its dead verdict to retireUnconfirmedBoot, which declines a confirmed claim, so the dead locator stayed recorded: at worker_cap 1 the slot leaked; at cap >= 2 the queue entry was dropped as stale and the task orphaned; the architect heard only worker-queued. Reproduced with the reviewer's /tmp/legion-60-repro/ready-close.test.ts at REPRO_CAP=1 and 2 before the fix (locator kept, readyConfirmedAt set, promptFailures 1, launchFailures undefined).
findings.fix: PromptNotStarted carries reason: "no-turn" | "socket-closed" (process-errors.ts). awaitTurnStart answers socket-closed when the socket closed before or during its wait — a flag set from client.closed is consulted after the confirming get_state too, so a close that made get_state fail is socket-closed, not no-turn (processes.ts). On socket-closed the ready path confirms, cancels, and queues nothing and logs one line (`…; boot left unconfirmed for the socket-close handler to retire`), leaving the claim an unconfirmed boot with its pendingAssignment; onWorkerClientClosed -> retireUnconfirmedBoot (queued behind the same role lock) is then the single handler: locator cleared and slot released, launchFailures counted, task re-queued and relaunched cold with --resume (worker-started), worker-died at the threshold. No prompt site counts a socket close against promptFailures (queueUnstartedPrompt takes the reason; promoteQueuedWorker's catch skips recordPromptFailure for it) — on the queued and direct paths markWorkerDead alone retires the worker — and promptExistingWorker leaves no late-start continuation on a closed socket's receipt.
tests: processes.test.ts: `retires a ready-time worker whose socket closes after acknowledging its first task and relaunches the task cold with --resume (workerCap 1)` and `(workerCap 2)` — built from the reviewer's repro on workerCapFixture with a fake tmux that reports a new pane per launch; assert the dead pane %301 is killed, the claim is relaunched as %302 at generation 2 unconfirmed with the task kept, launchFailures 1 and promptFailures untouched, the relaunch argv carries --resume=<session file>, the queue is empty, and the architect hears exactly [worker-started] (never worker-queued)

processes.test.ts: `does not count a socket that closes during a queued promotion's wait as a prompt failure: the task stays queued and the next drain re-prompts the reconnected worker` — the reconnect-succeeds variant, where the old code counted promptFailures 1 against a live worker

findings.finding: awaitTurnStart's get_state-failed branch returned not-started without consulting receipt.hasStarted, so an agent_start that arrived while get_state was failing produced a spurious promptFailures count, a spurious worker-queued on the direct paths, two persists, and a misleading late-start log line before commitLateStart committed.
findings.fix: receipt.hasStarted is consulted after the get_state call however it ended (processes.ts awaitTurnStart); the doc comment says so.
tests: processes.test.ts: `credits a turn that starts while the confirming get_state is failing, counting no prompt failure` — get_state emits agent_start then rejects; the prompt commits with promptFailures 0, one worker-started, no worker-queued, no console.error

rounds.fix: processes.test.ts: both cases now await the relaunch's worker-started publish through a publishRole hook resolving a Promise.withResolvers — the idiom the queued-promotion tests (e.g. `promotes the queued worker once the running one goes idle, publishing worker-started`) already use for exactly this real-I/O-before-tmux race. worker-started is published by promoteQueuedWorker only after launchWorker resolved (fresh claim written, token dequeued, persisted), so every assertion is deterministic behind it; a wait that never resolves fails on bun's own test timeout with the assertions unreached, never a false green. No assertion loosened or removed; the publications array the assertions read is the hook's own.
